rules.statement: Keep an OpenTofu component to one concern with no platform-, environment- or vendor-account-specific defaults; make every such value an input variable.
rules.why: Components are reusable building blocks; baking platform specifics into them prevents reuse across environments and self-hosters.
rules.check: Look for hard-coded account IDs, regions, domain names, ARNs or environment names in a component module's resources or variable defaults.

rules.statement: Lay out an OpenTofu component as `versions.tf` (only the `terraform` block), `variables.tf`, `main.tf` (locals, data sources, resources), `outputs.tf`, a snake_case `tests/<component>.tftest.hcl`, and a `README.md`.
rules.why: A uniform file layout lets every component be read and reviewed the same way.
rules.check: Check a new or changed component for resources or variables placed outside their designated file, extra blocks in `versions.tf`, a missing test file or README, or a test file not in snake_case.

rules.statement: Name the sole or primary resource of a type `this` and any other resource by its role in snake_case, and name module calls in a root by role in snake_case.
rules.why: Consistent naming makes resource addresses predictable across components and roots.
rules.check: Look for primary resources not named `this`, or secondary resources and module calls with generic, numbered or non-snake_case names instead of a role name.

rules.statement: In OpenTofu code, write comments that explain why (a provider quirk, a security choice, a constraint), never what the next line does.
rules.why: Comments restating the code add noise; the reasoning behind non-obvious choices is what readers need.
rules.check: Look for comments that merely paraphrase the following resource or attribute.

rules.statement: Format OpenTofu files with `tofu fmt` (two-space indent, aligned `=`).
rules.why: Canonical formatting keeps diffs minimal and consistent.
rules.check: Look for misaligned `=`, tabs or non-two-space indentation in .tf or .tftest.hcl files.

rules.statement: Give every OpenTofu variable an explicit `type` and a `description` that is a sentence ending in a period with literals in backticks, and give every output a `description`.
rules.why: Typed, documented inputs and outputs feed the generated docs and prevent misuse.
rules.check: Look for `variable` blocks missing `type` or `description`, descriptions without a trailing period or with unquoted literals, and `output` blocks without `description`.

rules.statement: Make OpenTofu variable defaults the secure choice (deletion protection on, most restrictive data classification, longest deletion window), and give required inputs no default.
rules.why: Secure-by-default components protect callers who don't override settings.
rules.check: Look for defaults that weaken security or durability (e.g. `deletion_protection = false`, short deletion windows, permissive classification) or placeholder defaults on inputs that should be required.

rules.statement: Constrain every OpenTofu input whose valid values are narrower than its type with a `validation` block whose `error_message` names the variable and states what it must be.
rules.why: Invalid inputs should fail at plan time with a clear message instead of at apply or in the provider.
rules.check: Look for variables with restricted valid values (enums, formats, ranges, lengths) lacking `validation`, or error messages that don't name the variable and the requirement.

rules.statement: Mark a secret OpenTofu input `sensitive = true` and document that its value comes from an environment variable or a secret store, never a committed file.
rules.why: Secrets must not appear in plan output or be committed to the repository.
rules.check: Look for secret-looking variables (passwords, tokens, keys) without `sensitive = true`, or tfvars/committed files supplying secret values.

rules.statement: Have an OpenTofu component take a `tags` variable (`map(string)`, default `{}`), merge its own `component`, `role`, `data_classification` and `deletion_protection` tags over the caller's in `local.tags`, and apply `local.tags` to every taggable resource.
rules.why: One consistent tag set on every resource supports ownership, classification and protection visibility.
rules.check: Look for components without a `tags` input, a merge order that lets caller tags override the component's, missing standard tag keys, or taggable resources not using `local.tags`.

rules.statement: Use snake_case tag keys with static values in OpenTofu resources, never timestamps, commit SHAs or other per-run values.
rules.why: Static tags keep plans from drifting; provenance comes from attestations and audit logs instead.
rules.check: Look for tag values computed from `timestamp()`, git SHAs, run IDs or other changing data, and for non-snake_case tag keys.

rules.statement: Give every stateful OpenTofu component a `deletion_protection` (`bool`, default `true`) input that drives the provider's own safeguards and a conditional `terraform_data` guard with `prevent_destroy = true` whose input is the primary resource's ID.
rules.why: `prevent_destroy` can't take a variable, so a count-gated guard resource makes any plan destroying the protected component fail.
rules.check: Look for stateful components (keys, buckets, databases, zones) lacking `deletion_protection`, lacking the count-gated `deletion_guard` resource, or enabling force-destroy/hard delete regardless of the flag.

rules.statement: When a refactor moves or renames an OpenTofu resource or module, add a `moved` block so existing state follows it.
rules.why: Without a `moved` block the resource is destroyed and recreated instead of keeping its state.
rules.check: Look for changed resource or module addresses in a diff without a corresponding `moved` block.

rules.statement: In reusable OpenTofu components, set `required_version = ">= 1.13.0"` and provider constraints `">= <floor>, < <next major>"`, where the floor is the first provider release supporting every resource and attribute used.
rules.why: Components should accept the widest compatible range without admitting provider versions that lack used features or break on a major release.
rules.check: Look for component provider constraints without a lower floor, without an upper major bound, with `~>` pins, or with a floor older than a used resource/attribute's introduction.

rules.statement: In live OpenTofu roots, use `required_version = "~> <minor>"` matching the repository's pinned OpenTofu version, `~>` provider constraints, and a committed `.terraform.lock.hcl` with checksums for every platform.
rules.why: Deployed roots need reproducible, exactly pinned toolchains across CI and developer platforms.
rules.check: Look for live roots with open-ended version constraints, a required_version that doesn't match the pinned OpenTofu version file, or a lock file missing or lacking multi-platform hashes.

rules.statement: When adding or raising an OpenTofu or provider version, pin the latest upstream release as read from the registry or release feed at that moment.
rules.why: Pinning from memory or docs yields stale versions.
rules.check: Look for newly added or raised versions that are older than the latest release at the time of the change.

rules.statement: In live OpenTofu roots, consume components only by a git source pinned to a released tag (`?ref=vX.Y.Z`), never a local path or branch.
rules.why: The hosted platform must run only the published artifacts it offers self-hosters.
rules.check: Look for module `source` values that are local paths, lack `?ref=`, or reference a branch or commit instead of a release tag.

rules.statement: Configure an OpenTofu `s3` backend with `use_lockfile = true` and an `encryption` block enforcing `aes_gcm` with a KMS key provider for both `state` and `plan`.
rules.why: State and plans contain sensitive data and must be locked and encrypted at rest.
rules.check: Look for backends without `use_lockfile = true`, or missing/partial `encryption` blocks that don't enforce encryption for both state and plan.

rules.statement: Configure OpenTofu providers in `providers.tf` with credentials from the environment only, with a comment naming the variable that supplies them and where CI reads it from.
rules.why: Credentials must never be committed, and readers need to know where they come from.
rules.check: Look for credentials or keys in provider blocks or tfvars, provider blocks outside `providers.tf`, or missing comments on credential sources.

rules.statement: Gate an OpenTofu `import` block for adopting existing infrastructure behind a variable that tests set to `false`.
rules.why: Mocked providers can't import, so ungated imports break plan-based tests.
rules.check: Look for `import` blocks without a controlling variable, or tests that don't disable it.

rules.statement: In OpenTofu tests, declare `mock_provider` for every provider, a top-level `variables` block with minimal valid inputs, and name each `run` in snake_case for the behavior it proves with `command = plan`.
rules.why: Tests must run offline without real credentials and read as a list of proven behaviors.
rules.check: Look for tests using real providers, runs using `command = apply`, missing top-level variables, or run names that don't describe a behavior.

rules.statement: In OpenTofu tests, write each `assert` `error_message` as the rule that broke, using "must".
rules.why: A failing assertion should state the violated requirement directly.
rules.check: Look for assert messages that describe the observed value or are vague instead of stating what must hold.

rules.statement: Cover in an OpenTofu component's tests the secure defaults, the tag merge over caller tags, that `deletion_protection = false` removes the guard, and every `validation` block with an `expect_failures = [var.<name>]` run.
rules.why: These are the component's safety guarantees and must not regress silently.
rules.check: For each added validation, default or protection change, look for a corresponding run; flag validation blocks without an `expect_failures` run.

rules.statement: When mocking an attribute of nested type in an OpenTofu test, supply every one of its fields.
rules.why: OpenTofu rejects partial nested mocks with "Invalid mock/override field".
rules.check: Look for `mock_resource`/`override_*` defaults setting nested-type attributes with only some fields.

rules.statement: Give every OpenTofu component and root a `README.md` with its purpose and rationale, a bullet list of behaviors and safeguards, and an `hcl` usage example whose `source` ends in `?ref=<version>`, followed by the terraform-docs section.
rules.why: Consistent docs explain each module and show how to consume it by released version.
rules.check: Look for new modules or roots without a README, or READMEs missing the purpose, behaviors list, or a version-pinned usage example.

rules.statement: Never hand-edit the section between `BEGIN_TF_DOCS` and `END_TF_DOCS`; regenerate it with terraform-docs when variables or outputs change.
rules.why: The section is generated and CI checks it matches the code.
rules.check: Look for manual edits inside the generated markers, or variable/output changes without a regenerated docs section.
